On the right, layout_spectral() places the nodes by two eigenvectors of the graph's Laplacian, which recovers the grid: nine nodes in three rows of three, joined to their neighbors." width="100%"} The coordinates of each node are its entries in the eigenvectors of the second and third smallest eigenvalues of the Laplacian `L = D - A`. These vectors are the smoothest non-constant functions on the graph, so adjacent nodes get similar coordinates: the layout shows the global shape (rings, grids, the two halves of a barbell) cleanly, but it can crowd dense regions into a small area. The result is centered and scaled so the largest coordinate is `scale=`. This matches NetworkX's `spectral_layout()`, up to the sign of each axis, which is fixed here so that the first node with a nonzero coordinate has a positive one. Edge direction is ignored (directed graphs use `A + A^T`), parallel edges add up and self-loops are skipped. A disconnected graph has several zero eigenvalues, so its components collapse onto a few points; lay out components separately or use a force-directed layout instead. Graphs of 400 nodes and more use a sparse eigensolver. Graphs with one or two nodes have no third eigenvector: one node goes to `center=`, two nodes to either side of it. Positions are stored as `[x, y]` lists in the `attr_name=` node attribute; see `layout_circular()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[bool]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, use edge weights (`1` where missing) as adjacency entries. If `False`, every edge counts `1`. If `None` (default), follows whether the graph was created as weighted. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Largest coordinate after rescaling. `None` keeps the raw eigenvector entries (`center=` is then ignored). Default is `1.0`. [center]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [(0.0, 0.0)]{.doc-parameter-default} : Center of the layout, as `(x, y)`. Default is the origin. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node attribute to store the positions in.
